exposure: emergency C/S at a gestational age of less than 36 weeks
estimated blood loss more than 2000 ml
outcome: Maternal morbidity (ICU admission, blood transfusion >6 units, hysterectomy)
cohort: 230 women diagnosed with placenta previa at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, from January 2001 to December 2013
finding: Placenta previa is a leading cause of maternal morbidity, and risk factors for morbidity include complete previa, previous C-section, emergency C-section before 36 weeks, and blood loss exceeding 2000 ml.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was performed in 56.5% of women with placenta previa as an emergency procedure and in 43.5% as elective.
